new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the penultimate syllable; stress is not listed among the contrastive features (four vowels, seventeen consonants, no length).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Revel 1995. Note however Thiessen 1981:10 (quoted in Zorc's PJL review, file p.109): 'Word accent in Q[uezon], B[rooke's] P[oint], C[anipaan], and M[olbog] falls on one of the last two syllables of a word, including both suffixed and unsuffixed forms... In none of the languages are words distinguished by accent alone so accent is not contrastive'; and Zorc (same review): accent differences in Brooke's Point 'are the result of Tagalog or Bisayan superstrata and often differ from one idiolect to another'.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word in a dictionary-introduction phonology sketch (citation forms implied); no discussion of phrase-level prominence or of suffixed forms (Thiessen's second-hand statement explicitly includes suffixed forms within the last-two-syllable window).
new_statements.identity_note: Revel's 'Palawan' (1979 grammar; 1995 CAD chapter) is the highland Pala'wan of the Mäkägwaq and Tämlang valleys in Brooke's Point municipality (her own field site, stated in Revel 2021/2022, The Rosetta Project/archive.org filed the excerpt under ISO plc (Central Palawano = cent2090) and Glottolog attaches Revel-Macdonald 1979 to the Nuclear Palawan node (nucl1738), but the described variety corresponds to broo1239. Thiessen 1981's accent statement (known only via Zorc's review) is a joint statement for Quezon (plc), Brooke's Point (plw), Canipaan (Southwest Palawano, plv) and Molbog (pwm). Zorc's unpublished field data (informant 'Ibis Maringit', locality not stated) are labelled simply 'Palawano'.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1984-85 [Zorc's list: 1983c]. Review of Thiessen, Henry Arnold. 1981. Phonological reconstruction of Proto-Palawan. Philippine Journal of Linguistics 15(2)-16(1): 109-111. (scan from zorc.net; scanned with tesseract)
sources.note: p.109: quotes Thiessen 1981:10: 'Word accent in Q[uezon], B[rooke's] P[oint], C[anipaan], and M[olbog] falls on one of the last two syllables of a word, including both suffixed and unsuffixed forms... In none of the languages are words distinguished by accent alone so accent is not contrastive on this level and is not written.' Zorc adds (first-hand): 'my own data on Aborlan, Brooke's Point, and Batak indicate that accent differences are the result of Tagalog or Bisayan superstrata and often differ from one idiolect to another. Hence, Proto-Palawan probably had lost PPH accent.'

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. n.d. [1970s field notes, scanned 2012]. Palawano field data ('', 94 pp.: typed Palawano lexicon without accent marks; Proto-Austronesian reflex chart 'Palawano (Ibis Maringit)'; typed and handwritten elicited sentences and vocabulary with accent marks). Unpublished, zorc.net/RDZorc/Palawano/.
sources.note: No prose statement. Transcriptions mark accent: in sentences mostly on the final syllable (itúŋ, sədáʔ, pərák, buyáŋ, tinapáy, bəgás, ugasán) and in vocabulary on the penult when it has a full vowel (ságəd, dágəs, mən-ándəl, págud, mə-lámma) but on the ultima when the penult is schwa (ləpiníg, mən-aráp, rəpók). Raw data only; sampled pp. 1-4, 22-41, 25, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90-94.
